plants.name: Tulsi
plants.habitat: Native to the Indian subcontinent. Grows in tropical and subtropical regions up to 1800m altitude. Thrives in full sunlight.
plants.description: Tulsi is revered as the 'Queen of Herbs' in Ayurveda and holds a sacred place in Hindu tradition. This aromatic shrub is a cornerstone of traditional Indian medicine, used for millennia to treat a wide spectrum of ailments. Its adaptogenic properties help the body cope with stress while its antimicrobial compounds fight infections.

stem.name: Stem
stem.description: The stem of Tulsi is square-shaped, purple or greenish, and covered with fine hairs. It is woody at the base and herbaceous at the top.
benefits: Contains eugenol — a potent anti-inflammatory compound
Stem decoction relieves throat infections and hoarseness
Used in Ayurvedic formulations for fever management
Anti-bacterial properties against E. coli and S. aureus
Stem paste applied to insect bites for instant relief
stem.preparation: Boil 10–12 Tulsi stems in 2 cups of water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink warm with honey.

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Tulsi leaves are oval with serrated edges, bright green, and release a strong aromatic scent when crushed due to essential oils like eugenol, methyl eugenol, and caryophyllene.
benefits: Powerful adaptogen — reduces cortisol and stress
Boosts immunity by increasing T-helper cell and NK cell activity
Expectorant — clears congestion and relieves cough
Rich in Vitamin C, Vitamin A, and antioxidants
Anti-diabetic — lowers fasting blood glucose
Reduces anxiety and promotes mental clarity
leaf.preparation: Chew 5–7 fresh leaves each morning on an empty stomach, or brew as tea with ginger and black pepper.

flower.name: Flowers
flower.description: Tulsi produces small purple or white flowers arranged in dense spikes (racemes). The flowers have a honey-like fragrance and are rich in essential oils.
benefits: Potent anti-malarial properties documented in research
Flower tea relieves headaches and migraines
Helps in managing scorpion and snake venom effects (traditional use)
Rich in flavonoids — powerful antioxidants
Used in aromatherapy for stress relief
flower.preparation: Steep 1 tablespoon of dried Tulsi flowers in hot water for 5 minutes. Add honey and drink.

root.name: Root
root.description: The roots of Tulsi are fibrous and light brown. They possess unique medicinal properties distinct from the aerial parts.
benefits: Traditional treatment for malaria and periodic fevers
Root powder mixed with honey treats ringworm and skin infections
Anti-rheumatic — relieves joint pain and arthritis
Diuretic properties support kidney health
Used to treat snakebite (traditional emergency remedy)
root.preparation: Dry roots, grind to fine powder. Mix 1/2 teaspoon with warm water twice daily for joint pain.

immunity: Boosts T-cells and NK cell count
Adaptogenic — counters physical and mental stress
respiratory: Relieves asthma, bronchitis, and chronic cough

cultivation.soil: Well-drained, fertile loamy soil with pH 6.0–7.5
cultivation.climate: Tropical and subtropical, 20°C–35°C. Cannot tolerate frost.
cultivation.watering: Moderate — water every 2–3 days. Avoid waterlogging.
cultivation.season: Best planted at onset of monsoon (June–July). Harvest before flowering.
cultivation.propagation: Seeds or stem cuttings. Germination in 7–14 days.

recipes.name: Tulsi Immunity Kadha
recipes.method: Boil all ingredients (except honey) for 10 minutes. Strain, cool slightly, add honey. Drink twice daily.
recipes.benefits: Boosts immunity, relieves cold and flu symptoms

recipes.name: Tulsi Skin Toner
recipes.method: Boil leaves in water for 15 minutes. Strain and cool. Mix with rose water. Apply with cotton pad.

plants.name: Ashwagandha
plants.habitat: Dry, arid regions of India (Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP). Also found in Mediterranean and Africa. Grows up to 1500m altitude.
plants.description: Known as the 'King of Ayurvedic Herbs', Ashwagandha is one of the most powerful adaptogens in existence. The Sanskrit name means 'smell of horse' — symbolizing the strength and vitality it imparts. Used for 3000+ years to combat stress, anxiety, and fatigue.

stem.name: Stem
stem.description: The stem is erect, branched, with a grayish-green color and covered with fine white hairs (tomentose). It is woody at the base.
benefits: Stem bark contains alkaloids with anti-inflammatory action
Decoction helps in respiratory conditions
Contains withanolides — potent bioactive compounds
Anti-microbial properties against gram-positive bacteria
Used in traditional poultices for carbuncles and ulcers
stem.preparation: Bark decoction: Boil 5g dried stem bark in 200ml water for 15 minutes. Drink 50ml twice daily.

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Simple, oval leaves with undulate margins. Bright green, larger in lower portions of the plant.
benefits: Anti-tumor properties — withanolides induce cancer cell apoptosis
Leaf paste applied to carbuncles and swellings
Anti-inflammatory — reduces pain and joint swelling
Febrifuge — reduces fever
Veterinary use for livestock health
leaf.preparation: Crush fresh leaves into a paste. Apply directly to inflamed joints or skin swellings.

flower.name: Flowers
flower.description: Small, greenish or dull yellow bell-shaped flowers appearing in clusters at leaf axils.
benefits: Flowers have diuretic properties
Used as emmenagogue in traditional medicine
Mild sedative effect — aids sleep quality
Anti-bacterial when applied topically
flower.preparation: Flower tea: Steep dried flowers in hot water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink before bedtime.

root.name: Root
root.description: The most important medicinal part — thick, fleshy taproot with a horse-like smell due to withanolides. Harvested in winter (Nov–Jan).
benefits: Powerful adaptogen — normalizes stress response (cortisol regulation)
Enhances thyroid function in hypothyroidism
Boosts testosterone and male fertility
Improves muscle mass and strength (studied in athletes)
Neuroprotective — may reduce Alzheimer's progression
Anti-diabetic — lowers blood sugar comparably to oral drugs
Reduces anxiety scores by 40% (clinical trials)
root.preparation: Mix 1 tsp (3-5g) root powder in warm milk with honey. Drink nightly for 90 days for best results.

cultivation.soil: Sandy loam to red, well-drained. pH 7.5–8.0. Tolerates poor soil.
cultivation.watering: Minimal — once a week. Overwatering causes root rot.
cultivation.season: Sow seeds in August-September. Harvest roots after 150-180 days.
cultivation.propagation: Seeds (fresh seeds germinate better). Sow 1-2 cm deep.
cultivation.spacing: 60 cm between plants, 90 cm between rows

recipes.name: Ashwagandha Golden Milk
recipes.method: Warm milk, whisk in all powders until smooth. Add honey. Drink 30 minutes before bedtime.
recipes.benefits: Deep sleep, stress relief, muscle recovery

plants.name: Neem
plants.habitat: Native to India and Myanmar. Grows throughout South Asia, Africa, and Caribbean. Thrives in tropical/subtropical regions with 400–1200mm annual rainfall.
plants.description: Called 'Sarva Roga Nivarani' (Curer of all diseases) in Sanskrit, Neem is one of the most versatile medicinal trees known. Every part — from bark to seed — has documented therapeutic properties. It is the world's most researched medicinal plant with thousands of scientific studies validating its traditional uses.

stem.name: Bark
stem.description: The bark is thick, grayish-brown, with deep longitudinal furrows. It is extremely bitter due to nimbin, nimbidin, and nimbidol.
benefits: Anti-malarial — bark decoction used for centuries against Plasmodium
Anti-ulcer — protects gastric mucosa
Reduces fever — traditional antipyretic
Treats jaundice and liver disorders
Bark paste relieves skin diseases including eczema and psoriasis
stem.preparation: Neem bark decoction: Boil 10g bark in 400ml water until reduced to 100ml. Drink 50ml twice daily.

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Compound leaves with 8–19 leaflets, lance-shaped with serrated margins. Young leaves are reddish, mature ones deep green.
benefits: Azadirachtin — powerful anti-bacterial and antifungal compound
Anti-diabetic — lowers blood sugar significantly
Dental health — neem twigs as toothbrush is an ancient practice
Acne treatment — reduces P. acnes bacterial count
Anti-parasitic — treats intestinal worms
Wound healing and scar reduction
leaf.preparation: Grind 20 fresh leaves with water into a smooth paste. Apply to acne or infected wounds. Or boil leaves for a medicinal bath.

flower.name: Flowers
flower.description: Small, white, highly fragrant flowers appearing in spring. Rich in flavonoids and essential oils.
benefits: Anti-viral — inhibits Herpes Simplex virus activity
Excellent for digestive health — eaten fresh in traditional cuisine
Reduces bile pigments — treats jaundice
Anti-spasmodic — relieves intestinal cramps
Flower extract shows anti-fertility effects (traditional contraceptive)
flower.preparation: Eat 20-30 fresh flowers in the morning to purify blood and support liver. Cooked with jaggery in Ugadi festival.

root.name: Root
root.description: Neem roots are bitter and contain high concentrations of tetranortri terpenoids. The root bark is the most potent part.
benefits: Root bark extract: powerful anti-inflammatory and analgesic
Traditional treatment for snake and scorpion bites
Anti-malarial — stronger than leaf extracts
Expectorant — loosens chest congestion
Root decoction treats burning urination (UTI)
root.preparation: Root bark decoction (very bitter): 5g dried root bark in 200ml water. Boil for 20 minutes. Take 30ml with warm water.

cultivation.soil: Almost any soil type — clay, loam, sandy. pH 6.2–8.5. Very adaptable.
cultivation.watering: Very minimal once established. Grows in rain-fed conditions.
cultivation.season: Year-round. Seeds sown in monsoon. Fast-growing — 3-5m in first year.
cultivation.propagation: Fresh seeds (viability drops quickly). Also from stem cuttings.

recipes.name: Neem Face Pack
recipes.method: Mix all ingredients into a smooth paste with rose water. Apply to face for 15 minutes. Rinse with cool water.
recipes.benefits: Reduces acne, brightens skin, antibacterial cleanse

plants.name: Turmeric
plants.habitat: Native to South and Southeast Asia. Requires tropical climate with 1500mm+ annual rainfall and temperatures 20°C–35°C. Grown extensively in India (world's largest producer).
plants.description: Turmeric is perhaps the most scientifically studied medicinal plant, with over 12,000 published papers on curcumin alone. Used for 4000+ years in Ayurveda as 'Haridra', it is simultaneously a spice, dye, cosmetic, and medicine. Its golden color comes from curcuminoids — the most powerful natural anti-inflammatory compounds known.

stem.name: Stem (Pseudostem)
stem.description: Turmeric has a false stem (pseudostem) formed by leaf sheaths. The true stem is underground. The pseudostem is tender and edible.
benefits: Pseudostem extract has anti-inflammatory compounds
Used in traditional medicine for fever reduction
Anti-oxidant properties in the leaf sheath extracts
Eaten as a vegetable in South India and Southeast Asia
Contains curcumin analogs with similar medicinal properties
stem.preparation: Chop fresh pseudostem finely. Use in cooking or blend into fresh green juice.

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Large, elongated leaves 35–75 cm long, bright green with distinct midrib. Used as food wrapper in South Indian cuisine (Patraveli).
benefits: Anti-inflammatory — contains curcumin-related compounds
Leaf extract is anti-cancer in preliminary studies
Traditional wound dressing — leaves wrapped around injuries
Antibacterial when used as food wrapping (preserves food)
Leaf oil used in aromatherapy for relaxation
leaf.preparation: Use fresh leaves to wrap and steam food — this infuses food with curcuminoids. Also used in Patraveli (leaf plate) cooking.

flower.name: Flowers
flower.description: Beautiful pale yellow or white tubular flowers appearing at the center of the plant. Edible and used in traditional cuisine.
benefits: Edible flowers rich in essential oils
Anti-inflammatory flavonoids
Traditional treatment for earache (flower juice)
Used in Thai and South Asian cuisine for color and aroma
Floral extract shows antibacterial properties
flower.preparation: Fresh flowers can be added to salads or cooked in curries. Flower juice: press 10 flowers, dilute with water, and apply 2-3 drops in ear for earache.

root.name: Rhizome (Root)
root.description: The underground rhizome is the primary medicinal part — bright orange-yellow inside due to curcuminoids. Pungent, bitter, and slightly peppery in taste.
benefits: Curcumin — most potent natural anti-inflammatory (inhibits NF-κB pathway)
Stronger than aspirin and ibuprofen for arthritis pain relief
Anti-cancer — induces apoptosis in multiple cancer cell lines
Anti-Alzheimer's — prevents amyloid plaque formation
Liver protective — regenerates hepatocytes
Accelerates wound healing by 3x (clinical evidence)
Lowers LDL cholesterol and prevents oxidative damage to arteries
root.preparation: Golden Milk: 1 tsp turmeric powder + pinch black pepper (piperine increases absorption by 2000%) + warm milk. Take daily.

digestive: Stimulates bile production — aids fat digestion

cultivation.soil: Deep, well-drained loamy or alluvial soil. pH 5.5–7.0. Rich in organic matter.
cultivation.watering: Regular irrigation every 7–10 days. Needs consistent moisture.
cultivation.season: Planted at beginning of monsoon (May–June). Harvested after 7–9 months.
cultivation.propagation: Rhizome pieces (15–25g each) with 2–3 buds. Plant 5–7cm deep.

recipes.name: Turmeric Golden Milk
recipes.method: Warm milk over low heat. Whisk in all spices. Do not boil. Add honey last. Drink nightly.
recipes.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, immune booster, sleep aid, cancer prevention

plants.name: Brahmi
plants.habitat: Grows in wet, marshy areas and along water bodies throughout India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, China, and Florida. Found at altitudes up to 1400m.
plants.description: Brahmi is Ayurveda's premier brain tonic and nervine herb, named after Lord Brahma — the Hindu god of creation and universal consciousness. Used for 3000+ years to sharpen intellect, improve memory, and treat epilepsy. Modern research confirms its remarkable neuroprotective and cognitive-enhancing properties.

stem.name: Stem
stem.description: Creeping, succulent stem that spreads along the ground and roots at nodes. Light green and highly branched.
benefits: Contains bacoside compounds along the entire stem
Anti-oxidant properties throughout aerial parts
Traditional treatment for skin disorders when applied as paste
Stem juice is a traditional hair tonic — prevents premature greying
Anti-inflammatory when consumed as tea
stem.preparation: Brahmi stem juice: Crush a handful of stems, extract juice. Mix with coconut oil (1:4) for hair application.

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Small, succulent, oblong leaves (4–6mm long), slightly notched at the tip. Arranged alternately on the stem. Bitter taste.
benefits: Bacosides A & B — enhance synaptic transmission and nerve signal speed
Increase BDNF (Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor) by up to 50%
Reduce anxiety by modulating serotonin and GABA receptors
Adaptogen — reduces cortisol and physiological stress response
Antiepileptic — reduces seizure frequency
Improve word recall and attention in clinical studies
Protect neurons from mercury and aluminum neurotoxicity
leaf.preparation: Chew 4–5 fresh leaves daily (bitter taste but highly effective). Or prepare Brahmi ghee: simmer leaves in clarified butter, strain, take 1 tsp daily.

flower.name: Flowers
flower.description: Small, white or light purple five-petaled flowers with 4 stamens. Appear throughout the year in favorable conditions.
benefits: Flower extract shows anti-epileptic properties
Mild sedative effect — aids sleep quality
Anti-oxidant flavonoids
Used in traditional formulations for mental clarity
flower.preparation: Brahmi flower tea: Steep 10–15 fresh or dried flowers in hot water. Add honey. Drink before meditation or study.

root.name: Root
root.description: White, fibrous roots at each node. The entire plant including roots is used medicinally in some preparations.
benefits: Root extracts show anti-cancer properties in preliminary studies
Contains alkaloids with anti-spasmodic activity
Traditional treatment for bowel disorders
Diuretic properties
root.preparation: Whole plant decoction (including roots): Boil 20g plant material in 400ml water. Reduce to 100ml. Take 50ml twice daily.

cultivation.soil: Waterlogged or very moist soil. Can grow in water (semi-aquatic). pH 6.0–7.0.
cultivation.climate: Tropical. Thrives in warm, humid conditions. 15°C–40°C.
cultivation.watering: Requires consistent moisture — grows naturally in marshy areas. Keep soil always wet.
cultivation.season: Year-round in moist conditions. Best growth in monsoon.
cultivation.propagation: Stem cuttings (very easy). Each node roots readily in moist soil.

recipes.name: Brahmi Brain Tonic
recipes.method: Warm milk, whisk in powders thoroughly. Add honey and cardamom. Drink every morning for 3 months.
recipes.benefits: Enhanced memory, focus, anxiety relief, better sleep

plants.name: Aloe Vera
plants.habitat: Originally from Arabian Peninsula. Now cultivated worldwide in tropical, semi-tropical, and arid regions. Highly adaptable — grows in pots, deserts, and gardens.
plants.description: Aloe Vera is the original 'miracle plant' — used by Cleopatra, Alexander the Great, and ancient Indian physicians alike. Its thick gel contains 75+ active compounds including vitamins A, C, E, B12, minerals, enzymes, and polysaccharides. It is simultaneously one of the world's largest cosmetic ingredients and a potent internal medicine.

stem.name: Stem
stem.description: Aloe Vera is a stemless or very short-stemmed plant. The apparent 'stem' is a compact rosette base from which leaves emerge.
benefits: The rosette base contains concentrated aloin
Traditional use in Unani for liver disorders
Anti-fungal properties at the base
Contains storage of water and nutrients
stem.preparation: The entire leaf base can be used. Split the base, extract the clear gel for topical use or internal consumption.

leaf.name: Leaf (Gel & Latex)
leaf.description: Thick, fleshy, lance-shaped leaves with serrated edges. Inside: clear mucilaginous gel (inner parenchyma) and yellow bitter latex (rind layer). The gel is the primary medicine; the latex (aloin) is a powerful laxative.
benefits: Gel: 99% water + 75 active compounds — supreme skin moisturizer
Sunburn relief — reduces redness and pain within hours
Accelerates wound healing — stimulates fibroblast growth
Anti-aging — increases collagen production and reduces wrinkles
Oral gel relieves mouth ulcers (aphthous stomatitis)
Anti-diabetic — lowers fasting blood glucose
Digestive aid — soothes IBS, acid reflux, and gastritis
Aloin (latex): extremely potent laxative — use cautiously
leaf.preparation: Fresh gel: Split leaf, scoop clear gel with spoon. Apply directly to burns/skin. For internal use: blend 2 tbsp gel in 1 glass water/juice. Take 20 minutes before meals.

flower.name: Flower
flower.description: Tubular orange or yellow flowers on a central spike (1 meter tall). Appear in spring/summer. Attracts birds and bees.
benefits: Flower nectar is edible and rich in antioxidants
Traditional medicine uses flowers for menstrual problems
Anti-inflammatory properties in flower extracts
Used in Ayurvedic formulations for blood disorders
flower.preparation: Flower tea: Steep 10 fresh or dried Aloe flowers in hot water for 8 minutes. Add honey.

root.name: Root
root.description: White, fibrous roots that store water. Usually kept in soil, not harvested.
benefits: Root extracts show anti-bacterial properties
Traditional treatment for skin diseases in Ayurveda
Anti-tumor compounds in root extracts
root.preparation: Root decoction (rare): Boil 5g dried roots in 200ml water for 10 minutes. Use topically for skin infections.

immunity: Rich in Vitamin C, E, and beta-carotene

cultivation.soil: Sandy, well-drained, poor soil is preferred. pH 7.0–8.5. Excellent drainage is critical — root rot is the main killer.
cultivation.climate: Arid to semi-arid. Tolerates 10°C–40°C. Cannot survive frost. Full sun.
cultivation.watering: Minimal — water deeply but infrequently (every 2–3 weeks). Allow complete drying between waterings.
cultivation.season: Year-round in warm climates. Indoor plant in cold regions.
cultivation.propagation: Offsets/pups (baby plants) that appear around the base. Simply separate and replant.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera Detox Drink
recipes.method: Scoop fresh Aloe gel, blend smoothly. Mix with all ingredients. Drink on empty stomach each morning for 30 days.
recipes.benefits: Gut healing, skin glow, detoxification, weight management

plants.name: Giloy
plants.habitat: Widely distributed across tropical India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka. A climbing vine found in forests, hedges, and gardens. Thrives when climbing Neem trees.
plants.description: Called 'Amrita' (nectar of immortality) in Sanskrit, Giloy achieved global recognition during COVID-19 for its extraordinary immune-modulating properties. This heart-leafed vine has been central to Ayurvedic medicine for 2000+ years, prescribed for fevers, immune weakness, and as a rasayana (rejuvenating herb).

stem.name: Stem
stem.description: The stem is the primary medicinal part of Giloy. It is thin, twining, with long aerial roots. The stem is fleshy, grayish-brown outside with white inside.
benefits: Tinosporin and berberine — powerful immunomodulators
Primary treatment for chronic fever (including dengue and malaria)
Anti-malarial — stem extracts inhibit Plasmodium growth
Stem juice reduces dengue platelet destruction
Hepatoprotective — protects liver from alcohol and toxins
Anti-diabetic — improves insulin sensitivity
Anti-gout — reduces uric acid levels
stem.preparation: Giloy stem juice: Crush 6-inch stem piece, extract juice with water. Take 20-30ml twice daily. Or prepare kadha (decoction).

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Beautiful heart-shaped (cordate) leaves, 5–7 cm across, bright green and smooth. Similar to paan (betel) leaf in shape.
benefits: Anti-inflammatory — inhibits pro-inflammatory cytokines
Antioxidant — high DPPH radical scavenging activity
Immunomodulatory — increases macrophage activity
Antipyretic — traditional fever management
Anti-rheumatic — reduces joint inflammation
leaf.preparation: Fresh leaf juice: Blend 10 leaves with water. Strain and drink 30ml daily. Or dry and powder leaves.

flower.name: Flowers
flower.description: Small, yellow, unisexual flowers appearing in spring on separate male and female plants.
benefits: Flower extract has antimicrobial properties
Traditional fever management
Mild diuretic properties
flower.preparation: Flower tea: Steep dried flowers in hot water. Take as a general tonic.

root.name: Root
root.description: Yellowish, bitter roots with starchy pith. The root is used in Unani preparations.
benefits: Anti-rheumatic — traditional treatment for arthritis
Antipyretic properties
Liver protective
Anti-helminthic (deworms)
root.preparation: Root decoction: Boil 5g dried roots in 200ml water for 15 minutes. Take 50ml twice daily.

cultivation.soil: Any well-drained soil. pH 6.5–7.5. Grows best near Neem trees (Gil from Neem trees is considered most potent).
cultivation.climate: Tropical. 25°C–40°C. Cannot tolerate frost. Partial shade acceptable.
cultivation.watering: Moderate irrigation. Established vines are drought-tolerant.
cultivation.season: Plant stem cuttings in rainy season (June–July). Grows vigorously.
cultivation.propagation: Stem cuttings (10–15 cm) — very easy to propagate. Plant with support structure.

recipes.name: Giloy Immunity Kadha
recipes.method: Crush Giloy stem and ginger. Boil all ingredients in 1 cup water for 10 minutes. Strain, add honey. Drink warm twice daily during fever or illness.
recipes.benefits: Fever reduction, immune boost, platelet increase in dengue

plants.name: Amla
plants.habitat: Native to tropical India. Widely distributed in Myanmar, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Malaysia. Grows in subtropical mountain forests and dry deciduous forests.
plants.description: Amla is the richest natural source of Vitamin C on Earth — containing 20x more than oranges. In Ayurveda, it is the most important single ingredient in Chyawanprash and Triphala — two of the most prescribed formulations. Named 'Amalaki' (meaning nurse) in Sanskrit, it is described as the ultimate rasayana (rejuvenating agent).

stem.name: Bark
stem.description: The bark is grayish-brown, peeling in thin flakes. The inner bark is reddish with a bitter taste.
benefits: Bark decoction treats skin diseases including eczema
Anti-inflammatory — reduces swelling
Antipyretic properties
Traditional treatment for gonorrhea (Unani)
Wound healing — tannins in bark help coagulation
stem.preparation: Bark decoction: Boil 10g bark in 400ml water. Reduce by half. Apply externally for skin diseases or drink 50ml for fever.

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Very small, feathery, light green leaves arranged alternately — resembling a fern. When the tree sheds leaves, it looks spectacular like 'autumn leaves'.
benefits: Leaf juice treats conjunctivitis and eye inflammations
Anti-diarrheal — astringent tannins
Anti-dysenteric properties
Leaf decoction for rinsing mouth — anti-gingivitis
Hair rinse with leaf water promotes hair growth
leaf.preparation: Leaf decoction: Boil a handful of fresh leaves in 500ml water for 10 minutes. Use as hair rinse or eye wash.

fruit.name: Fruit
fruit.description: Small, round, greenish-yellow fruit with 6 vertical ridges. Extremely sour, astringent, and bitter with a sweet aftertaste. Contains the highest natural Vitamin C density.
benefits: 700–900mg Vitamin C per 100g (heat-stable unlike synthetic Vit C)
Boosts collagen synthesis — anti-aging
Triphala (Amla + Haritaki + Bibhitaki) — the world's most researched herbal formula
Improves iron absorption by 67% (critical for anemia)
Lowers LDL cholesterol — prevents arteriosclerosis
Anti-diabetic — reduces HbA1c
Powerful hepatoprotective — treats jaundice and fatty liver
Strengthens all 7 dhatus (tissues) of the body
fruit.preparation: Eat 1–2 fresh Amla daily. Or Amla juice: 30ml fresh juice + water + honey, morning. Amla murabba (preserved in sugar) is a traditional daily supplement.

root.name: Root
root.description: Yellowish-brown roots with medicinal bark. Less commonly used than fruit.
benefits: Root bark treats jaundice in traditional medicine
Anti-ulcer properties
Diuretic — treats urinary disorders
Traditional treatment for dysentery
root.preparation: Root bark decoction: 5g bark in 200ml water, boiled for 15 minutes. Take 50ml for jaundice.

cultivation.soil: Rocky, well-drained soil. pH 6.5–9.5. Highly adaptable to marginal lands.
cultivation.climate: Tropical and subtropical. 10°C–45°C. Very drought-tolerant once established.
cultivation.watering: Minimal once mature. Young trees need regular irrigation.
cultivation.season: Planted in July–August. Fruits appear in winter (December–February).
cultivation.propagation: Budding or grafting (for early fruiting). Seeds take longer.

recipes.name: Amla Hair Oil
recipes.method: Heat coconut oil, add Amla and other ingredients. Simmer until Amla blackens. Strain and store. Massage into scalp weekly.
recipes.benefits: Prevents greying, strengthens roots, promotes growth

plants.name: Peppermint
plants.habitat: Originally a hybrid of watermint and spearmint. Grows in moist soil near streams and water bodies. Cultivated worldwide, especially in India, US, Europe. Found at altitudes up to 2000m.
plants.description: Peppermint's primary compound, menthol, triggers cold receptors in the skin and mucous membranes — creating the characteristic cooling sensation without actually lowering temperature. Used across Ayurveda, Unani, and Homeopathy, peppermint is one of the oldest and most versatile medicinal herbs, documented in ancient Egyptian papyri dating to 1000 BCE.

stem.name: Stem
stem.description: Square stem (characteristic of all mints), reddish-purple in color, with opposite pairs of leaves. Highly aromatic when crushed.
benefits: Contains menthol throughout the stem
Steam inhalation with peppermint stem relieves nasal congestion
Anti-microbial — inhibits growth of common pathogens
Analgesic when applied topically as compress
stem.preparation: Add crushed peppermint stems to boiling water. Inhale steam with towel over head for 10 minutes for sinus relief.

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Oval, toothed leaves, dark green above and pale below. Rich in menthol (40–55% of essential oil) and menthone. Intense cooling aroma.
benefits: Menthol — activates cold receptors (TRPM8) without lowering temperature
IBS treatment — enteric-coated peppermint oil reduces abdominal pain by 40%
Tension headache relief — topical menthol equals paracetamol in studies
Antibacterial against H. pylori (ulcer-causing bacteria)
Antifungal against Candida albicans
Improves exercise performance — increases blood oxygen saturation
Anti-nausea — motion sickness and morning sickness
leaf.preparation: Peppermint tea: Steep 10 fresh leaves in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drink after meals for digestion. For headache: crush 2 leaves and rub on temples.

flower.name: Flowers
flower.description: Tiny lilac/purple flowers in whorls around the stem. Appear in midsummer. Bees love peppermint flowers.
benefits: Flower extract is strongly antimicrobial
Rich in flavonoids and rosmarinic acid
Anti-inflammatory properties
Relaxant — mild sedative effect in tea
flower.preparation: Peppermint flower tea is a delicate, gently sedating brew. Steep 1 tablespoon dried flowers in hot water for 7 minutes.

root.name: Root (Rhizome)
root.description: Peppermint spreads via underground runners (rhizomes). The rhizome is the primary means of propagation.
benefits: Rhizome contains concentrated essential oils
Traditional treatment for digestive cramping
Anti-spasmodic
Diuretic in Unani medicine
root.preparation: Rhizome decoction: Boil fresh rhizomes in water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink for digestive issues.

cultivation.soil: Moist, rich, well-drained loam. pH 6.0–7.0. Prefers organic-rich soil.
cultivation.climate: Cool to warm. 18°C–25°C ideal. Tolerates mild frost.
cultivation.watering: Regular watering — keep consistently moist. Mulch to retain moisture.
cultivation.season: Spring planting. Harvest before flowering for maximum menthol content.
cultivation.propagation: Stem cuttings or root division (easiest). Root in water, then transplant.
cultivation.spacing: 30–45 cm (spreads aggressively — use containers to control)

recipes.name: Peppermint Digestive Tea
recipes.method: Pour boiling water over fresh leaves. Cover and steep for 5 minutes. Add lemon and honey. Drink after meals.
recipes.benefits: Relieves bloating, gas, IBS pain, improves digestion

plants.name: Calendula
plants.habitat: Native to Mediterranean region. Now cultivated worldwide as an ornamental and medicinal plant. Grows in temperate to cool climates.
plants.description: Calendula's bright orange flowers have been used medicinally since ancient Rome and Greece. In Homeopathy, it is known as the 'rescue remedy for wounds' — one of the most prescribed remedies for cuts, bruises, and surgical wounds. In Unani medicine, it is 'Zergul', prescribed for inflammatory conditions. Modern research confirms its exceptional wound-healing, anti-inflammatory, and antifungal properties.

stem.name: Stem
stem.description: Branching, hairy, sticky stem with a strong aromatic smell due to terpenoids. Greenish with reddish tinge near base.
benefits: Stem extracts are anti-inflammatory
Contains resin with wound-healing properties
Anti-microbial essential oils throughout the stem
Traditional use for treating skin irritations
stem.preparation: Crush fresh stem and apply directly to minor wounds as a first-aid measure.

leaf.name: Leaves
leaf.description: Alternate, oblong, slightly hairy leaves with smooth margins. Light to medium green. Young leaves are edible in salads.
benefits: Anti-inflammatory compounds including saponins and flavonoids
Wound healing when applied as poultice
Anti-microbial against Staphylococcus
Young leaves edible — add to salads
Leaf extract helps regulate menstrual cycles
leaf.preparation: Fresh leaf poultice: Crush fresh leaves and apply directly to minor wounds, bruises, or skin irritations. Replace every few hours.

flower.name: Flower
flower.description: Large, bright orange or yellow daisy-like flowers with multiple ray and disc florets. The PRIMARY medicinal part — rich in flavonoids (quercetin, isorhamnetin), triterpenoids, carotenoids, and essential oils.
benefits: Calendula cream/ointment — clinically proven for wound healing (better than petroleum jelly)
Anti-fungal against Candida albicans
Anti-bacterial against MRSA (antibiotic-resistant staph)
Reduces dermatitis and diaper rash (pediatric studies)
Anti-tumor — lymphocyte activation against cancer cells
Estrogenic activity — regulates menstrual irregularities
Conjunctivitis eye wash (anti-inflammatory)
In Homeopathy: Calendula 30c is the primary wound and surgery remedy
flower.preparation: Calendula tea: Steep 2 tbsp dried flowers in boiling water for 10 minutes. Drink or use as wound wash. Calendula oil: Infuse dried flowers in coconut oil for 4–6 weeks for topical use.

root.name: Root
root.description: Fibrous, yellowish-white roots. Less commonly used than flowers.
benefits: Anti-inflammatory root extracts
Traditional treatment for fever
Emmenagogue — stimulates menstrual flow
root.preparation: Root decoction for fever: Boil 5g dried roots in 200ml water for 15 minutes. Take 50ml twice daily.

cultivation.soil: Well-drained, moderately fertile soil. pH 5.5–7.0. Tolerates poor soil.
cultivation.climate: Cool to temperate. 10°C–25°C. Frost-tolerant and heat-tolerant.
cultivation.watering: Moderate — water when top inch of soil is dry.
cultivation.season: Plant in early spring or fall. Blooms for months continuously.
cultivation.propagation: Direct seed sowing. Germinates in 5–10 days. Self-seeds readily.

recipes.name: Calendula Wound-Healing Oil
ingredients: 2 cups coconut oil or olive oil
recipes.method: Place dried flowers in a clean jar. Cover completely with oil. Seal and place in sunny window for 4–6 weeks. Strain with cheesecloth. Apply to wounds, dry skin, eczema, or use as massage oil.
recipes.benefits: Wound healing, scar reduction, anti-inflammatory skin therapy
